title: A modest defense (and partial critique) of the viral Wicked review #W...
transcript: So this review of wicked is going viral for saying that the plot lines involving the talking animals and Nessa Rose are not critical to Wicked Part 1. And while a lot of people are hating on this reviewer, I'm actually gonna defend it a little bit, because while I don't agree with their sentiment at all, I do get where they're coming from. And the first thing that I'll say is that you should not be required to have familiarity with a piece of media before you go and see the movie adaptation. Movies should stand on their own. And I don't think it is fair to criticize this critic for not having seen the stage musical or knowing what is going to happen in part two. And I think that he is right to say that Nessa Rose does not have a ton to do in this movie, and that's certainly an issue with the stage show as well. And when the entire payoff of this character comes in part two, I totally get why someone would leave part one wondering why that character was there. That is, unfortunately, where my defense of this review stops, because he then goes on to say that by cutting those plot lines, they could have just fit the whole musical into one film. And when you clearly have not seen the musical, I don't think that is a statement you could make. He also says that the talking animal subplot is Superfluous. And that is just insane to me, because even if you ignore part two and just focus in on part one, that plot line is so important to the overall narrative, not only plot wise and thematically, but also informing Elphaba's character and her character development throughout the film. And if his perspective was that that wasn't given enough attention and that they should have flushed it out more than I may be able to see, that side, to imply that the solution is to just cut it entirely, I think, is completely insane and misses the point of the entire movie.
